lessons.title: Some, Any, A/An: Determiners for nouns
lessons.content: Use 'some' with uncountable and plural countable nouns in affirmative sentences. Use 'any' with uncountable and plural countable nouns in negative sentences and questions. Use 'a/an' with singular countable nouns; use 'an' before vowel sounds.

details.explanation: We use 'some' with uncountable nouns and with plural countable nouns, in affirmative sentences.
details.example: We have got some water. I have got some apples.
details.burmese: 'some' ကို uncountable nouns နဲ့ plural countable nouns တွေမှာ affirmative sentences တွေမှာ သုံးပါ။

details.explanation: We use 'any' with uncountable nouns and with plural countable nouns, in negative sentences and questions.
details.example: I haven't got any milk. He hasn't got any apples. Have you got any orange juice? Are there any bananas?
details.burmese: 'any' ကို uncountable nouns နဲ့ plural countable nouns တွေမှာ negative sentences နဲ့ questions တွေမှာ သုံးပါ။

details.explanation: We use 'a/an' with singular countable nouns in affirmative and negative sentences and in questions. 'An' goes before a vowel sound.
details.example: I haven't got a burger. He has got an egg. Have you got an MP3 player?
details.burmese: 'a/an' ကို singular countable nouns တွေမှာ သုံးပါ။ vowel sound ရှေ့မှာ 'an' ကို သုံးပါ။
